observed_facts.fact: H-5 OHLCV technical features showed IC ~0.02-0.04 in Phases 9-13 but failed to generalize
H-3 macro regime features showed highest IC (~0.13-0.15) but temporal instability
Phase 17A walk-forward: no candidate positive across all 8 windows
Phase 16 portfolio: Sharpe +0.016 vs equal-weight baseline (not economically meaningful)
Path structure (H-1), return asymmetry (H-2), volatility dynamics (H-4) all classified FRAGILE
All 4 macro features CLIFF-sensitive; inflation 2022 regime destructive
Phase 17C-R null calibration: Ridge train IC +0.032, val/test IC ~+0.001

inferences.inference: H-5 label may be too short for OHLCV technical information to produce robust signal
Macro information may operate at longer horizons than H-5
Walk-forward instability suggests regime dependence, not pure horizon mismatch
Economic translation is the binding constraint, not statistical signal

speculations.speculation: Longer horizons (H-10, H-20) may show stronger signal for macro features
Shorter horizons (H-1) may be too noisy for OHLCV features
Cross-sectional features may be more horizon-robust than time-series features

key_question: Could weak/null predictive results be partly explained by horizon mismatch?
diagnosis_principle: The purpose is to test and attempt to falsify the horizon-mismatch explanation, not to confirm it.
